script: I brought his precious stone, and the teacher did something unimaginable.. I was in 4th grade, 1980s, and I just moved to a new elementary school. I left my best friend behind. He handed me a thumb‑sized cat's eye stone as a goodbye gift—his most prized possession, so it felt like a piece of his soul. (I knew, right?) The teacher set up a "Show and Tell" and everyone brought the usual fluff. I pulled out the stone. It lit up the room. Kids stared. The gem was a total eye‑catcher for a 10‑year‑old. I felt like royalty. After class, the teacher slid me over. She squinted at the stone and said, "Can I borrow it? I'd love to show the other teachers." I was a good kid, so I handed it over. (Totally naïve.) That was the last time I saw that stone. Months later, I begged the teacher to give it back. She shrugged, "I'll give it back next time, sweetie." "Next time" never happened. (Honestly, the audacity.) Then my mom came to a school event. I begged her to intervene. She politely told the teacher I wanted the stone back. The teacher just nodded, smiled, and promised—yet she kept the stone. She played dumb, assuming an 80s kid and a polite parent wouldn't stir a scene over a "little rock." (Like, seriously.) She stole my most precious keepsake just because she wanted it. Even now, decades later, I replay that helpless, clueless kid in my head. The injustice is scarier than losing my best friend. (Literally insane.) How do you even think you're entitled to rob a child of their treasured memory? I'd rather have my own voice than a teacher who thinks she's above the law.
